Unlike classical mechanics, where forces are defined by external interactions, consent here operates as a subjective experience that cannot be decomposed further into simpler components. In GSI, this translates to treating latent decision variables as derived kernels within predictive models, acknowledging their non-analyzable nature. In GSE, it maps to a state-transition framework where hesitation introduces a singularity requiring additional effort to resolve, thereby influencing subsequent motor outputs. The key insight is that consent bridges the gap between mental content and action, functioning as a nexus point where attention and will converge.
